answer: Each agent could earn influence only after posting a bond that is slashed if an audited task fails or the same operator is caught controlling supposedly independent accounts. Auditors randomly replay tasks and compare behavior across accounts, so a sybil farm must either keep its agents costly and genuinely distinct or risk losing collateral. An oasis of cheap identities therefore brings little weight; the ivory cost is locked capital, while varied outputs must avoid the echo that exposes shared control.
